reasoning: Roofline reports compute bottleneck with Compute SOL 92.0% vs Memory SOL 42.1%. Kernel metrics match: sm__throughput 91.95% and dram__throughput 42.13%, with full warp activity (100%), indicating arithmetic pipelines—not DRAM—are the primary limiter.

root_causes.cause: Very high FP/VALU instruction pressure from fused FC1 + SiLU + FC2 accumulation dominates runtime.

evidence.interpretation: SM compute pipelines are near saturation, leaving little compute headroom.

fixes.fix: Reduce instruction count by increasing math efficiency (e.g., restructure dot-product loops to improve data reuse and replace expensive scalar ops where possible), and evaluate MFMA/tensor-core style lowering paths for supported dtypes.
fixes.rationale: When compute is ~92% of peak, only fewer instructions per output or faster math units can materially improve performance.

root_causes.cause: Register-heavy kernel configuration (116 VGPR/thread) in a deeply fused kernel increases per-thread execution cost and limits further scheduling flexibility.

evidence.interpretation: High register footprint is consistent with large fused live state, making the kernel harder to optimize beyond current compute ceiling.

fixes.fix: Tune Triton tile sizes/unrolling (BLOCK_J, BLOCK_OUT, num_warps, num_stages) to lower live ranges and register usage, even if it slightly increases memory traffic.
fixes.rationale: In a compute-bound kernel, reducing register pressure can improve instruction scheduling/latency hiding and raise effective ALU utilization.
